key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca3PX3 strongly tunes the optoelectronic response, with Ca3PI3 emerging as the most promising photovoltaic candidate.
engineering_relevance: This suggests composition engineering can be used to optimize perovskite solar absorbers for higher efficiency and targeted device performance.
method: First-principles calculations of structural, electronic, and optical properties.
Band-structure analysis to determine bandgap type and magnitude.
SLME-based photovoltaic screening to compare solar-cell efficiency across F, Cl, Br, and I variants.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps from 2.0 to 3.788 eV and SLME results showing Ca3PI3 at 29.6% efficiency versus only 0.6% for Ca3PF3.
watch_item: The reported efficiencies come from theoretical screening, so experimental stability, defect tolerance, and fabrication feasibility still need validation.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
